## Why? {#why}

**Research question:** Can someone else (or you yourself in a year, for the revision) produce the same tables and numbers from the raw data of the simulator study with a single command?

Reviewers ask for the code, journals for open data, and the revision arrives months later on a new computer with new package versions. Reproducible means: same data + same code + same environment = same result. This does not take big tools, just a few habits: one project folder with a fixed structure, paths with here, pinned package versions with renv, randomness with a seed, version control with git and a report that is created from the code.

- **Project folder:** One RStudio/Positron project (`.Rproj`) per study. Raw data in `data/raw/` are never changed; cleaned data and results are created by scripts in `data/processed/` or `output/`. Number the scripts (`01-clean.R`, `02-models.R`), put functions in `R/`.
- **Paths with here:** `here::here("data", "raw", "survey.csv")` works throughout the project, whether you work in the console, with `Rscript` or while rendering a report in `reports/`. `here::i_am("analysis/01-clean.R")` at the top of the script fixes the root. No `setwd()`.
- **renv:** `renv::init()` creates a project library, `renv::snapshot()` writes the packages in use with their versions to `renv.lock`, `renv::restore()` restores them on another computer. renv finds packages by *reading* the code, not running it.
- **Randomness:** `set.seed()` once before the first random step (allocation, bootstrap, simulation, imputation); also save allocation schedules as a file.
- **git:** Every meaningful change as a commit with a short message; generated files in `.gitignore`. A tag such as `submitted-2026-10` marks the submitted state.
- **Report from code:** A Quarto document reads the data, computes and writes tables and numbers itself (lesson Reporting results). `quarto render` recreates everything.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## More: targets, Docker, preregistration

- **targets** builds an analysis pipeline as a dependency graph and, after a change, recomputes only the affected steps; worth it for long computations (bootstraps, Bayesian models).
- **Docker/rocker** additionally pins the operating system and system libraries; renv plus `sessionInfo()` in the appendix is usually enough.
- **Preregistration:** Write the analysis script on simulated data before data collection and deposit it on OSF with the commit hash; after collection, only swap the file.
- **Sharing data:** Anonymise raw data (no names, dates of birth; check free text), include a codebook (lesson Importing data).
:::

## Example {#example}

Create a small project in the browser file system, set the working directory to a subfolder and still read and write from the root:

```{webr}
proj <- file.path(tempdir(), "demo-study")
dir.create(file.path(proj, "data", "raw"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(proj, "analysis"), showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines("Version: 1.0", file.path(proj, "demo-study.Rproj"))
file.create(file.path(proj, "analysis", "01-clean.R"))
write_csv(driving_sim, file.path(proj, "data", "raw", "driving_sim.csv"))
setwd(file.path(proj, "analysis"))

here::i_am("analysis/01-clean.R")
here::here("data", "raw", "driving_sim.csv")
raw <- read_csv(here::here("data", "raw", "driving_sim.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
nrow(raw)
```

`here::i_am()` reports the root it found; every path starts there. Making randomness reproducible:

```{webr}
set.seed(2026)
sample(sprintf("p%02d", 1:24), 6)
set.seed(2026)
sample(sprintf("p%02d", 1:24), 6)   # same selection
```

## Package comparison {#packages}

| Task | Recommendation | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| Paths in the project | **here** `here()`, `i_am()` | rprojroot (the basis of here); not `setwd()` |
| Package versions | **renv** `init()`, `snapshot()`, `restore()` | groundhog (packages by date); Docker/rocker for the whole system |
| Version control | **git** (terminal, RStudio/Positron), usethis `use_git()` | OSF file versions |
| Report from code | **Quarto** `quarto render` | R Markdown; papaja for APA manuscripts |
| Pipelines | targets | Makefile; numbered scripts with one `run-all.R` |

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Run locally: set up a project with renv and git

The browser has neither a project library nor git. Locally, once per project:

```r
usethis::create_project("~/studies/driving-study")   # .Rproj and folders
renv::init()                                          # project library
usethis::use_git()                                    # git repository, first commit
# ... write the analysis, install packages ...
renv::snapshot()                                      # update renv.lock
```

In the terminal (or in the Git pane of RStudio/Positron):

```bash
git add analysis/01-clean.R renv.lock
git commit -m "Exclude participants failing the attention check"
git tag submitted-2026-10
```

On a new computer: clone the repository, open the project, `renv::restore()`, then `quarto render reports/report.qmd`.

One report for several subsamples or study waves: set parameters in the header of the Quarto document and when rendering instead of copying the document.

````markdown
---
title: "Report"
format: docx
params:
  wave: 1
---

```{r}
data <- readr::read_csv(here::here("data", "raw", "survey.csv")) |>
  dplyr::filter(wave == params$wave)
```
````

```bash
quarto render reports/report.qmd -P wave:2 --output report-wave2.docx
```
:::

## Cheat sheet {#cheatsheet}

```r
# At the top of every script
here::i_am("analysis/01-clean.R")
library(dplyr)                                    # load packages explicitly
raw <- readr::read_csv(here::here("data", "raw", "survey.csv"))
dir.create(here::here("output"), showWarnings = FALSE)
set.seed(2026)                                    # before the first random step

# renv (local)
renv::init(); renv::snapshot(); renv::restore(); renv::status()
renv::dependencies()                              # what renv finds in the code

# Read the lockfile
lock <- jsonlite::read_json("renv.lock")
purrr::map_chr(lock$Packages, "Version")

# Never: setwd("C:/..."), overwrite raw data, library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
```
